questions.question: In a periodic-review single-item inventory system with backlogging, period $k$ starts with inventory level $I_k$ (after any delivery), faces demand $D_k$ and ends with inventory position $P_k'$; $I_{k+1}$ is the next start level. Which indicator does the ready rate $\alpha$ average over $k=1,\dots,n$?
options: $\mathbf{1}\{I_{k+1}\ge0\}$, the next start level after any delivery
$\mathbf{1}\{I_k\ge0\}$, the start level before the demand
$\mathbf{1}\{I_k-D_k\ge0\}$, the level left after the demand
$\mathbf{1}\{P_k'\ge0\}$, the end position including orders

questions.question: In a periodic-review single-item inventory system with backlogging, the ready rate $\alpha$ over periods $1,\dots,n$ is the fraction of periods that end with a non-negative inventory level $I_k'$. One period starts with $I_k=3$ and has demand $D_k=3$, so the shelf is exactly empty at its end. How does this period enter $\alpha$?
options: It counts as ready and adds $1/n$, since no customer is left waiting
It counts as not ready, since an empty shelf is a stockout
It is left out of both the numerator and the denominator
It counts as half a ready period, adding $1/(2n)$ to $\alpha$

questions.question: In a periodic-review single-item inventory system with backlogging, a shop measures the ready rate $\alpha$, the fraction of periods $1,\dots,n$ whose end-of-period inventory level is non-negative, and finds $\alpha=0.9$. What does $1-\alpha=0.1$ measure?
options: The fraction of all demanded units that had to be backlogged
The fraction of replenishment cycles that ended with a backlog
The fraction of periods that started with an empty or negative shelf
The fraction of periods that ended with customers still waiting

questions.question: In a periodic-review single-item inventory system with backlogging, the ready rate $\alpha=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{k=1}^n\mathbf{1}\{I_k'\ge0\}$ averages, over periods, an indicator of the state at each period end. For a queue with number in system $L(t)$, which performance measure has the same structure?
options: The arrival-average probability: the fraction of arrivals that find $n$ in the system
The time-average probability $p(n)$: the long-run fraction of time with $L(t)=n$
The time-average number in system: the long-run average of $L(t)$ itself
The queue drift $\lambda-\mu$: the expected change of the queue length per period

questions.question: In a periodic-review single-item inventory system with backlogging, the end-of-period levels $I_1',\dots,I_n'$ are random, and the ready rate over these periods is the random variable $\alpha=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{k=1}^n\mathbf{1}\{I_k'\ge0\}$. What is $\mathbb{E}[\alpha]$?
options: $\frac{1}{n}\sum_{k=1}^n\mathbb{P}(I_k'\ge0)$
$\mathbf{1}\{\frac{1}{n}\sum_{k=1}^n\mathbb{E}[I_k']\ge0\}$
$\prod_{k=1}^n\mathbb{P}(I_k'\ge0)$
$\frac{1}{n}\sum_{k=1}^n\mathbb{E}[(I_k')^+]$

questions.question: In a periodic-review single-item inventory system with backlogging, five periods start with inventory levels $I_k=5,2,4,3,6$ and have demands $D_k=3,4,2,5,2$. What is the ready rate $\alpha$, the fraction of periods whose end-of-period level $I_k-D_k$ is non-negative?
options: $\alpha=1$
$\alpha=2/5$
$\alpha=3/5$
$\alpha=3/4$

questions.question: In a periodic-review single-item inventory system with backlogging, over $10$ periods, $2$ periods have zero demand and start with stock on hand, $6$ periods have positive demand and end with a non-negative level, and $2$ periods have positive demand and end with a backlog. What is the ready rate $\alpha$ over the $10$ periods?

In a periodic-review single-item inventory system with backlogging, a shop wants a ready rate of at least $0.95$ over $60$ periods, where the ready rate is the fraction of periods that end with a non-negative inventory level. At most how many of the $60$ periods may end with a backlog?

In a periodic-review single-item inventory system with backlogging, period $3$ ends with inventory level $I_3'=-3$ (three units backlogged). An order of $5$ units placed at the start of period $3$ with lead time $l=1$ arrives at the start of period $4$, and period $4$ has demand $D_4=1$. What is the end-of-period level $I_4'$?

In a periodic-review single-item inventory system with backlogging, a shop measures a ready rate (fraction of periods ending with a non-negative level) of $0.9$ over the first $20$ periods and of $0.8$ over the next $30$ periods. What is the ready rate over all $50$ periods?

In a periodic-review single-item inventory system with backlogging, a shop chooses its policy parameters to minimise the long-run average cost, with holding cost $h$ per unit on hand and backlog cost $b$ per unit backlogged per period, where $h$ is much larger than $b$. What ready rate $\alpha$ should be expected at the cost-minimising parameters?
options: Close to one, since every backlogged unit is penalised
Exactly $0.5$, where holding and backlog costs balance
The same as when $b$ is much larger than $h$
Close to zero, since stock costs more than backlog

questions.question: In a periodic-review single-item inventory system with backlogging, with lead time $l\ge1$ and orders outstanding, an analyst counts a period as ready when the end-of-period inventory position $P_k'$ (level plus units on order) is non-negative, instead of the end-of-period level $I_k'$. How does this count compare with the true ready rate $\alpha$?
options: It is never above $\alpha$, since the position subtracts backlog
It is never below $\alpha$, since $P_k'\ge I_k'$ in every period
It equals $\alpha$, since position and level differ by a constant
It equals $\alpha$, since every order is eventually delivered

questions.question: Under a base-stock policy with level $S$ and lead time $l=1$, starting from $I_1=S$ with nothing on order, period $k\ge2$ ends with $I_k'=S-D_{k-1}-D_k$, so it is ready exactly when $D_{k-1}+D_k\le S$. Why does the previous demand $D_{k-1}$ appear?
options: The units reordered for $D_{k-1}$ are still in transit during period $k$
Period $k-1$ always ends with a backlog of $D_{k-1}$ carried into period $k$
With $l=1$, the demand of period $k-1$ is only recorded in period $k$
The order placed at the start of period $k-1$ is still in transit then

questions.question: In a periodic-review single-item inventory system with backlogging, period $1$ starts with $I_1=4$ and nothing on order. The only order, of $6$ units, is placed at the start of period $2$ with lead time $l=2$, so it arrives at the start of period $4$. Demands in periods $1$–$5$ are $2,3,0,2,1$. What is the ready rate $\alpha$ over periods $1$–$5$?
options: $\alpha=4/5$
$\alpha=1/5$
$\alpha=3/5$
$\alpha=2/5$

questions.question: Under a base-stock policy with level $S=5$, ten periods end with inventory levels $I_k'=2,-1,0,-3,1,-1,3,-2,0,-1$. On the same demand path, raising the level to $S=6$ raises every end-of-period level by exactly $1$. What is the ready rate $\alpha$ (fraction of periods with $I_k'\ge0$) at $S=6$?
options: $\alpha=1$

questions.question: Under a base-stock policy with lead time $l=0$, every order arrives at once, so each period starts at level $S$ and ends with $I_k'=S-D_k$. On a recorded path of ten demands $3,6,2,4,5,3,8,4,2,5$, what is the smallest $S$ whose ready rate (fraction of periods with $I_k'\ge0$) is at least $0.9$?

In a periodic-review single-item inventory system with backlogging, a replenishment cycle runs from a period in which a delivery arrives up to the period before the next delivery, so no delivery arrives inside a cycle; demands are non-negative. The last period of some cycle ends with $I'\ge0$. What follows for the ready-rate indicators $\mathbf{1}\{I_k'\ge0\}$ of the earlier periods of that cycle?
options: All of them equal $1$, because the level cannot rise within a cycle
Nothing: an earlier period may end in backlog that is cleared later
Only the first period is sure to be ready, since the delivery came then
All of them equal $1$, but only when the lead time is $l=0$

questions.question: Under a base-stock policy with level $S$, lead time $l$, $I_1=S$ and nothing on order, period $k>l$ ends with $I_k'=S-(D_{k-l}+\dots+D_k)$. On the same demand path and the same $S$, the lead time grows from $l$ to $l+1$. How do the ready-rate indicators of periods $k>l+1$ change?
options: None changes, because the inventory position is still $S$
Some may turn from $1$ to $0$, and none can turn from $0$ to $1$
None can turn from $1$ to $0$, yet some may turn from $0$ to $1$
Every indicator of a period with positive demand turns to $0$

questions.question: In a periodic-review single-item inventory system with backlogging, periods $1$–$8$ end with levels $I_k'=3,1,-1,4,2,1,5,-2$; deliveries arrive at the starts of periods $4$, $7$ and $9$, each closing a replenishment cycle. Find the ready rate $\alpha$ (share of periods with $I_k'\ge0$) and the cycle service level $\alpha_c$ (share of cycles whose last period ends with $I'\ge0$).
options: $\alpha=3/4$ and $\alpha_c=1$
$\alpha=1/3$ and $\alpha_c=3/4$
$\alpha=3/4$ and $\alpha_c=1/8$
$\alpha=3/4$ and $\alpha_c=1/3$

questions.question: Under a base-stock policy with level $S=6$ and lead time $l=1$, period $k$ ends with $I_k'=S-D_{k-1}-D_k$. Demand repeats the pattern $1,4,2,5$ forever ($D_1=1$, $D_2=4$, $D_3=2$, $D_4=5$, $D_5=1$, …). What is the long-run ready rate, the limit as $n\to\infty$ of the fraction of periods $1,\dots,n$ with $I_k'\ge0$?
